sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match the columns or one word).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) Panchmel ki sabzi is a ________ cuisine. (b) Aviyal is a popular food of ________.
Fill in the blanks. (a) Suburban hotels are located on the ________ of cities and towns. (b) The word 'motel' is a short form of 'motor hotels'; this concept originated in ________.
Identify True or False. (a) Thai food is light and the herbs and spices used as common ingredients have medicinal value. (b) Hotels operate twenty-four hours a day for five days a week.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: they operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The state of India called the 'land of spices' is ________. (b) Sondesh is a popular dessert of ________.
Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Circuit house (b) Forest lodge. B: (i) Accommodation near wildlife sanctuaries (ii) Rooms for high-ranking government officials (iii) Cheap rooms for youth.
True or False. (a) A franchisee pays a fee to the franchisor. (b) A chain hotel has no common ownership.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: chain hotels are linked by a common hotel company.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Differentiate between commercial and non-commercial hospitality organisations.
questions.answer: Commercial organisations aim to earn profit, such as hotels, motels and resorts. Non-commercial ones give accommodation at very low rates or free, such as yatri niwas and dharamshalas.

questions.q: Explain how 'legal changes' impact the hospitality industry.
questions.answer: Changes in tax laws change the price of goods and services. Hotels may raise prices because of taxes such as VAT and service tax, which affects tourism.

questions.q: Explain how 'competition' impacts the hospitality industry.
questions.answer: Competition is affected by economic and regulatory factors, so hotels must watch rivals. After 9/11, airline restrictions reduced flying and hotels suffered.

questions.q: What is a franchise in the hotel industry?
questions.answer: A business agreement in which a franchisee pays a fee to a franchisor for the business name and management expertise.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Why is it important for hotels to meet a guest's expectations? List the guest expectations on arrival.
questions.answer: (i) Meeting expectations earns luxury status, guest satisfaction and repeat business. (ii) On arrival guests expect a warm welcome, well-groomed and communicative staff and quick check-in. (iii) They also expect clean rooms, efficient luggage handling by the bell desk and recognition by name.

questions.q: Explain any three expectations of guests during their arrival at the hotel.
questions.answer: (i) A warm and friendly greeting and welcome. (ii) An efficient and quick check-in with clean, well-maintained rooms. (iii) Efficient luggage handling by the bell desk from car to room.

questions.q: Differentiate between commercial and non-commercial organisations.
questions.answer: (i) Commercial organisations (hotels, motels, resorts) aim to earn profit. (ii) Non-commercial organisations (yatri niwas, dharamshalas, friends' homes) give low-cost or free service. (iii) Commercial ones cater to businessmen, tourists and families; non-commercial ones to budget travellers.

questions.q: Explain the classification of hotels on the basis of size and location (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Small hotels have under 25 rooms, medium 25–99, large 100–299 and very large over 300. (ii) Downtown hotels are in big cities for businessmen; suburban hotels are on the outskirts for meetings. (iii) Airport hotels serve transit guests, resorts are in forests or hill stations and motels are on highways.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the departments of a hotel and their main functions, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Front office assigns rooms, keeps room records, takes advance bookings and handles phone calls. (ii) Food and beverage service provides food in restaurants, room service, banquets and bars. (iii) Housekeeping keeps rooms clean and runs the linen room, laundry and gardening. (iv) Food production (kitchen) prepares dishes for guests, banquets and staff. (v) Administrative departments: maintenance, accounts, human resources and security. (vi) Purchase and stores buy and store goods (FIFO) and sales and marketing sell rooms and build the brand.

questions.q: Explain any six types of hotel classification with examples.
questions.answer: (i) Star classification from 1 to 5 stars by HRACC. (ii) By size: small, medium, large and very large. (iii) By location: downtown, suburban, airport, resort and motel. (iv) By guests: commercial and suite hotels. (v) By ownership (timeshare, condominium) and affiliation (chain, independent). (vi) By management (franchise, management contract) and supplementary accommodation (circuit house, dak bungalow, youth hostel, yatri niwas, forest lodge).
